biggest_catch: Only the first actionable report of a given issue is eligible — duplicates and already-known bugs pay nothing.
catches: Only the first actionable report of a previously-unknown issue is eligible — duplicates earn nothing.
Requires real security skill: finding a qualifying vulnerability takes expertise and often many hours.
Publicly disclosed bugs or reports to third parties typically do not qualify — coordinated disclosure required.
Only ever target your own accounts; testing others' data or disrupting users is prohibited.
Payouts vary by severity and report quality — most hunters earn nothing per report.

c1.evidence: Google's official bughunters repo publishes the VRP rules: bugs are reported through Google's vulnerability form, triaged by security engineers, and rewarded per the official reward table — a real, public, currently-maintained deal channel (rules updated ~11 days ago).

c2.evidence: Official rules publish reward examples from ~$240 (downgraded XSS) to $121,212 (exceptional RCE with quality multiplier); no fixed per-hunter range — framed as variable.

c3.evidence: Steps follow the official flow: research in scope, submit via the vulnerability form with PoC and impact, triage, reward decision.

c4.evidence: Reporting carries no upfront fee — open to anyone with a Google account.

eligibility: Anyone with a Google account and security-research skill; Google employees/contractors excluded.
notes: Scenario: security niche (bug bounty). Google's Vulnerability Reward Program pays researchers for valid, first-reported security vulnerabilities across Google products via bughunters.google.com. Highly skill-gated; payouts are per-report and variable — most reports earn nothing.
numeric_basis: payout: per-report rewards set by severity/quality, no fixed range (official examples ~$240-$121,212). time: reconnaissance + testing + writing a quality report, est. 90-240 min active.
payout_quote: Only the first actionable report of a given issue that we were previously unaware of is eligible.
payout_value_note: Rewards set per report by severity and quality (official examples ~$240–$121,212); no fixed per-hunter range — variable.

steps: Review the official VRP rules and in-scope products on Google's bughunters repo.
Research vulnerabilities in scope, targeting only your own accounts.
Submit a high-quality report via Google's vulnerability form: technical description, proof of concept, reproduction steps, and impact assessment.
Google's security team triages the report; if it is the first actionable report of a valid issue, a reward is set by severity and report quality.
timing: Reports are triaged continuously; rewards are paid after the report is validated.
